Package com.nexuslink.protocol.db

Enum Class SqlDialect

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<SqlDialect>
com.nexuslink.protocol.db.SqlDialect
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<SqlDialect>, Constable
public enum SqlDialect extends Enum<SqlDialect>
The SQL each engine actually accepts, chosen from the JDBC URL.

Statements the workbench generates for you — browsing a table, renaming a column, emptying a table, replacing a view — are not portable. LIMIT 100 is a syntax error on Oracle and SQL Server; SQL Server renames through sp_rename rather than ALTER TABLE; SQLite has no TRUNCATE; MySQL quotes identifiers with backticks and SQL Server with brackets. This enum keeps every one of those differences in one place, so the views can generate SQL without knowing which database they are talking to.

Pure and dependency-free: every method is a string transformation that can be unit-tested without a connection.

    • quote

      public String quote(String name)
      Quotes an identifier the way this engine expects — backticks on MySQL, brackets on SQL Server, double quotes elsewhere — doubling any embedded quote character. A name that is already qualified (schema.table) is quoted part by part, so the dot keeps its meaning.

    • stringLiteral

      public String stringLiteral(String value)
      A single-quoted string literal, embedded quotes doubled — the same on every engine here.

    • selectAll

      public String selectAll(String table, int rows)
      A "show me this table" statement capped at rows — what a double-click in the schema tree runs. Oracle and Db2 get FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY, SQL Server SELECT TOP (n), everyone else LIMIT n.

    • limitClause

      public String limitClause(Integer rows)
      The row-cap clause appended after ORDER BY, or an empty string on an engine that caps rows with a prefix instead — see topPrefix(Integer).

    • topPrefix

      public String topPrefix(Integer rows)
      The TOP (n) prefix that goes straight after SELECT, empty except on SQL Server.

    • supportsTruncate

      public boolean supportsTruncate()
      true when the engine has a real TRUNCATE TABLE. SQLite does not.

    • truncateTable

      public String truncateTable(String table)
      Empties a table: TRUNCATE TABLE where it exists, and an unfiltered DELETE on SQLite, which has no TRUNCATE.

    • renameTable

      public String renameTable(String table, String newName)
      Renames a table — sp_rename on SQL Server, RENAME TABLE on MySQL.

    • renameColumn

      public String renameColumn(String table, String column, String newName)
      Renames a column — sp_rename on SQL Server, RENAME COLUMN elsewhere. The RENAME COLUMN form needs MySQL 8.0 / MariaDB 10.5.2 or newer; older servers want CHANGE, which needs the column's full type and so cannot be generated from a name alone.

    • addColumn

      public String addColumn(String table, String column, String type)
      Adds a column. Oracle wraps the definition in parentheses and SQL Server omits the COLUMN keyword; the rest take ADD COLUMN.

    • dropColumn

      public String dropColumn(String table, String column)
      Drops a column. Oracle and SQL Server take no COLUMN keyword difference here.

    • dropObject

      public String dropObject(String kind, String name)
      Drops a table or view.
